$description: TURBINE design tokens. W3C Design Tokens Community Group draft format ($value / $type). Carries the values docs/CANON.md sections 4, 5 and 6 fix, plus one declared extension. Notes about the file live under $extensions, which the DTCG draft reserves for exactly this.

com.turbine.meta.about: Informational only. Nothing in here is a token: $extensions is outside the token tree by definition, so no build tool has to exclude it by name and no DTCG validator has to be told to ignore an invented $type.

project.note: Fictional electronic music festival. Teaching material for the WaysConf 2026 masterclass 'Build an AI that checks and fixes its own work'.

source.value: Figma — TURBINE file, Variables panel (the CANON-fixed subset)
source.note: This file carries the Figma variables whose values CANON fixes. It is not the whole Figma file: design/FIGMA-SPEC.md §12 records the Figma-only decisions — the five-step leading scale, tracking/wide, the 32px tablet gutter, and the border/*, size/* and responsive/* collections — as assumptions rather than canon, so scripts/build-figma-plugin.mjs carries those values and they stay out of this file until they are promoted to CANON. Figma is still upstream for everything that is here: change the variable there, change the value here, then run `node scripts/build-theme.mjs` and `node scripts/build-figma-plugin.mjs`.

naming.note: FIGMA-SPEC §2.1 is the naming authority for the Figma side. The mapping is not a plain dot-to-slash substitution in every group — spacing.6 is space/6, typography.fontSize.xl is text/xl, layout.maxWidth is size/content-max — so the executable statement of it is buildTokens() in scripts/build-figma-plugin.mjs, not the prose.

canon.note: Every colour, family, weight, size, spacing step, radius and breakpoint below is fixed by CANON, the shadow group excepted; see `extension`. If a value here disagrees with CANON, CANON wins.

format.value: W3C Design Tokens Community Group draft, $value / $type

theme.note: CANON section 4: dark theme is the only theme. There is no light palette and no theme switcher.

contrast.note: Computed WCAG 2.x contrast matrix for this palette, including the deliberate failures described in CANON section 8.

notTokenised.value: line-height, opacity, motion duration, easing, z-index
notTokenised.note: None of these is fixed by CANON, so none is exported here. Line height and the 10% hover opacity are fixed one level down, in FIGMA-SPEC §2.3 and §4, which FIGMA-SPEC §12 records as assumptions rather than canon; scripts/build-figma-plugin.mjs carries them so there is still exactly one place to change them. Motion duration, easing and z-index are fixed nowhere. To tokenise any of these, promote the value to CANON first, then export it here.

extension.note: The shadow group is the one group with no CANON counterpart, so it has no Figma variable either and sits outside the Figma-to-tokens name diff in FIGMA-SPEC §2.1 rule 5. Its colours are plain black at low alpha rather than palette values; AC-26 accepts them inside box-shadow and nowhere else, so #000000 never becomes a legal text colour.

color.$description: CANON section 4. Thirteen colours, dark theme only. The palette is built so that a careless implementation will fail contrast; see CANON section 8 and CONTRAST.md.

base.$description: Page background. Also the correct ink on accent and state fills.

subtle.$description: Hairlines, card borders. Decorative only: 1.45:1 on bg.base, below the 3:1 non-text bar, so it must never be the sole indicator of a control.

strong.$description: Focus ring base, dividers. 1.98:1 on bg.base: usable as an offset or underlay, never as the visible focus indicator on its own. See CONTRAST.md.

secondary.$description: Supporting copy. The correct choice wherever a muted grey is wanted.

muted.$description: Trap. CANON section 8. 4.07:1 on bg.base and 3.78:1 on bg.surface, both under the 4.5:1 normal-text bar, so even CANON's one permitted use — legal and footer text, set at 12px — would be a real axe failure. The built page therefore renders this token nowhere and sets the footer legal block in text.secondary; it stays in the palette because it is the colour a model reaches for, and reaching for it has to fail. See CONTRAST.md section 5, Trap 1.

on-accent.$description: Alias of bg.base. CANON section 4 fixes dark ink, not white, as the text colour on accent.sodium and on every other accent or state fill.

sodium.$description: Primary accent, sodium lamp orange, CTAs. Pair with text.on-accent, never with white.

typography.$description: CANON section 5. Three Google Fonts families and an eleven-step rem scale.

display.$description: Space Grotesk, Google Fonts. Weights 500 and 700. Display sizes carry letterSpacing.display; the wordmark carries letterSpacing.wordmark.

mono.$description: JetBrains Mono, Google Fonts. Weights 400 and 700.

normal.$description: Body copy and anything set in Inter or JetBrains Mono.

display.$description: Display sizes set in Space Grotesk.

wordmark.$description: The TURBINE wordmark only. All caps. Never rendered as 'Turbine Festival'.

spacing.$description: CANON section 6, in px: 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 · 32 · 48 · 64 · 96 · 128. Keys are multiples of the 4px base unit, so spacing.6 is 24px.

pill.$description: Fully rounded ends. Used for genre tags and the ticket badges.

breakpoint.$description: CANON section 6. These three widths are the only ones screenshotted and diffed by the validation step.

tablet.$description: The nav collapses to a hamburger below this width; the programme table stacks below it.

shadow.$description: Implementation extension. CANON sections 4 to 6 do not fix elevation, so these three steps have no Figma variable and sit outside the Figma-to-tokens name diff in FIGMA-SPEC §2.1 rule 5. On a near-black ground a shadow reads as absence of light, so each step is plain black at low alpha rather than a palette colour, with a long, soft spread. AC-26 accepts these three colours inside box-shadow and nowhere else. The $value is a DTCG composite so that the gate can read the colour field on its own; scripts/build-theme.mjs composes it into a CSS box-shadow string.

sm.$description: Resting cards and the sticky nav once it has scrolled.

md.$description: Hovered lineup cards, the open FAQ panel, the mobile nav sheet.

lg.$description: The highlighted Full Pass ticket card, lifted clear of the grid.
